title: Top-Down Bayesian Posterior Sampling for Sum-Product Networks

problem.claim: SPN structural constraints that enable fast inference increase learning-time complexity and can hinder the construction of highly expressive models.

gap.claim: An efficiently implementable Bayesian learning approach for large-scale SPNs is needed.

contributions.claim: A Gibbs-sampling full conditional probability is derived by marginalizing multiple random variables to obtain the posterior distribution more efficiently.
A hyperparameter-tuning method is proposed to balance prior-distribution diversity with optimization efficiency in large-scale SPNs.
A complexity analysis characterizes the sampling algorithm as efficient for the largest possible SPN.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method reportedly improves learning-time complexity and achieves computational speeds from tens to more than one hundred times faster in numerical experiments on more than 20 datasets.
The method reportedly achieves superior predictive performance in numerical experiments on more than 20 datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: SPNs provide exact and fast evaluation of fundamental probabilistic operations and are used in time- or accuracy-sensitive applications.
The structural constraints enabling efficient inference make learning more complex and may limit expressiveness.
The study develops Bayesian learning based on a marginalized Gibbs-sampling full conditional and adds hyperparameter tuning for large-scale models.
Complexity analysis reports efficiency even for the largest possible SPN.
Numerical experiments on more than 20 datasets report substantial speedups and superior predictive performance.

source_observation.claim: Marginalizing multiple random variables in a sampling update is reported to improve computational efficiency.

interpretation.claim: Analytically reducing sampling dimensionality may make Bayesian inference more practical for structured probabilistic models.

application.claim: When scaling Bayesian learning for structured models, consider deriving marginalized conditional updates before optimizing implementation details.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond SPNs or which model conditions are required.

source_observation.claim: The proposed tuning method balances prior diversity and optimization efficiency in large-scale SPNs.

interpretation.claim: Large-scale Bayesian model performance may depend on jointly managing prior exploration and optimization behavior.

application.claim: For large structured models, evaluate hyperparameter strategies against both diversity and optimization-efficiency objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the tuning procedure, objective formulation, or applicability to other model classes.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not specify the exact speedup measurement or predictive metrics.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or formal complexity bounds.
